key_insight: A high-order FR/CPR solver coupled with a rotating actuator-line model can predict VAWT aerodynamics accurately on fixed Cartesian grids without resolving blade geometry.
engineering_relevance: This geometry-free framework offers a computationally efficient tool for wind-turbine design studies, enabling fast parametric analysis and scalable simulations for large wind-energy systems.
method: Couple FR/CPR with a rotating actuator-line model to represent blade loading as volumetric body forces.
Project forces with an isotropic Gaussian kernel in a blade-attached frame.
Use a modified Boeing-Vertol dynamic stall model and DMST correction to recover physical inflow on coarse meshes.
evidence_signal: The method was validated against experimental near-wake measurements and LES-ALM results, with the power-coefficient curve matching high-fidelity 3D LES-ALM within 6% near optimal operating conditions.
watch_item: Accuracy on coarse meshes depends on a mesh-resolution criterion for the Gaussian kernel and careful handling of induction feedback with DMST correction.
paper_title: A High-Order Flux Reconstruction Actuator-Line Framework for Rotating-Blade Aerodynamics on Fixed Cartesian Grids
